chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The (Divine) Mercy is upon two aspects – the aspect of Wilayah and the aspect of intercession.

key_terms.التَّرَحُّمُ: Mercy or compassion, specifically referring to Divine Mercy in this context
key_terms.الشَّفَاعَةِ: Shafa'ah, referring to intercession on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةِ: Wilayah, referring to divine guardianship, authority, or leadership

ai.seo_question: What are the two aspects of Divine Mercy according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the dual aspects of Divine Mercy (Tarahhum) as rooted in Wilayah and Shafa'ah, reflecting the Shia theological framework where recognition of divine authority is intrinsically linked to the promise of intercession. This distinction underscores that mercy is not merely an abstract attribute but is operationalized through the spiritual hierarchy of the Imams, serving as both the source of guidance and the means of salvation for the faithful.
